title: Functions — practice quiz
description: A short check on writing functions, return types, `clampf`, and `await`. This quiz does not run GDScript; it only checks that the ideas landed.

choices: A labeled box that holds one value
A named recipe: a pack of steps you can run whenever you need them
A list of items in order
questions.explain: A function is a named pack of steps you can call whenever you need them, like `raise_fear()` or `toggle_flashlight()`. A labeled box that holds one value is a variable.

questions.prompt: In `func raise_fear(amount: float) -> void:`, what does `-> void` mean?
choices: The function returns a decimal number
The function must not be called
The function does not return a value
The function waits for a timer
questions.explain: `-> void` means the function does not give a value back. It just does work, like changing `fear`. A function that gives a decimal back would be written `-> float`.

choices: Keeps the new fear value between `0.0` and `max_fear`
questions.explain: `clampf` clamps a decimal number into a range. Here it stops fear from going below `0.0` or above `max_fear`.

choices: Closes the game after half a second
Pauses this function for half a second without freezing the whole game
questions.explain: `await` pauses only the function that uses it. The timer lasts half a second, then the function continues, while the rest of the game keeps running.
